title: Union rules, rehearsing acts and conventions
summary: DeDroit recalls union scales, his refusal to play acts he had not rehearsed, and the difficulty of convention shows.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger

blocks.x: Just put away, you see. Yeah. First dollar you ever made for talking.

Oh no, I made more than that. I'm kidding. I used to get $25 at Actors Masters Ceremonies. I know, I'm just kidding. In fly shows, you know. Yeah. They say, would you like to, would you like to master some? I said, certainly. I said, but you know the union rules. I said, what is it? I said, $25. It's all right. Boy, I know union rules. $25.

You could make up the rules as you went along. Listen, we're all made up rules to get out of tight spots, I'll tell you that. Yeah. I mean, impossible things. You know, they expect you to, you know, you know, you're not going to do it. I mean, the booking agents, you know, I had a booking agent, if the rehearsal would run over the, her time, which you wanted to put, I mean, the union used to allow an hour and a half, add it in with the floor show price, add it to the dance price. You see, you got paid for everything you did. You got paid for playing the show, and then if you rehearsed it, and you went over an hour and a half, you got. So she said, don't have any more overtime on rehearsal. I said, well that's very well. I said, but understand, I don't play any acts I don't rehearse. That floor, though, you're going to make an ass out of me. I'm standing on that floor telling me to play fast and slower and in front of all the people. And you've seen it done. Acts get out there and, you know what I mean, they don't work with you. If the orchestra made a mistake, well tell them afterwards. But I would never play an actor that I didn't rehearse. So I said, rehearsal time is up. Oh, I'm going to get out there and play a guy singing opera and I'll go through his music? I wonder what he's doing. And then some people take too much time. You take a fellow like, oh he's a big movie actor now, playing at the Rose Bowl, he'll have 50,000 cues, but he's a performer and you can play for those kind of people. They know what they're doing and they do it. You know what I mean? And they come up and say to me, thank you very much, you did a fine job. I don't want them to pat me on the back and hand me, I'm supposed to play the show right. Don't you think so? I had a fellow who did a wire actor, he and his wife, and he came over to me and he said, you know the spotlight man said, Judy, how are you doing it? I said, I am. He says, aren't Judy, Johnny was in the pit at the Orphian? I said, yes. And he took and he hugged me. He was an athlete. He said, Johnny, I haven't had my music played like you played it since God knows one. He said, most of the leaders don't even know what it means. At the finish of each trick it said applause segue. He meant, wait for the applause, and so he gets a breath, and then you pick up the next cue. So when I finished, and he went, and they deployed, then I get a pick up, he said, I felt like I was, you played forever. You know what I mean? Well I wasn't. You know what they do, they use a wall, they use a wall, they use a slack wire, you know. But the fact the man could work because he felt safe with the orchestra.

I've played some tough shows, I'm telling you boys, and you only get one crack at them when you play these conventions. They come right down from New York, they spend a million dollars to fly them here and everything else, but they don't give you any extra. You've got to get it before you start, that's all I want to tell you. And some of the music, terrific arrangements. I mean the biggest bands don't play an arrangement without rehearsing it, do they? No. I remember when I started with Bonnie Rao, his brother was, he used to put on that. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
